writingTips.title: Principle 1: Put the camera-move instruction first
writingTips.body: AI weights the beginning of a prompt more heavily. Write "orbiting shot, the frame circles…" before describing the scene. Never bury the camera move mid-paragraph or at the end.

writingTips.title: Principle 2: Define the start and end frames
writingTips.body: Don't just write "push in." Write "push from a wide shot to an eye close-up" — give the AI a clear starting picture and ending picture. The clearer both endpoints, the better the AI knows how to "walk."

writingTips.title: Principle 3: Add one speed word
writingTips.body: "Slowly push in" and "rapidly push in" are two entirely different emotions. Slow = tender, elegant, suspenseful. Fast = tense, impactful, startling. One speed word sets the tone.

writingTips.title: Principle 4: Camera move + mood keyword is the golden pair
writingTips.body: A camera move alone is a technical instruction; add a mood keyword and it becomes a creative one. E.g. "slow push-in, heavy suffocating atmosphere", "orbiting shot, epic ceremonial feel". Together they help the AI grasp the feeling, not just the motion.

writingTips.title: Principle 5: At most 1–2 camera moves per prompt
writingTips.body: For a clip under 15 seconds, 1–2 moves are already rich. Pile on more and the AI loses track, muddying the frame. For complex shot language, split into multiple generations and stitch in post.

usageAdvice.headline: For clips under 15 seconds, stick to 1–2 camera moves — the footage will be steadier.
rest: Pick a camera move first, then replace the bracketed subject, scene, mood, and style in the template.
When copying a prompt, keep the four ingredients — start, end, speed, mood — and results usually stay controllable.

slopIntro: Community consensus: abstract "vibe words" leave the model unable to tell which element to emphasize. Break vibe words into the physical elements that create the feeling — texture, light, color, air — and the image immediately stabilizes.

slopTraps.good: Write shot size, camera move, light source, and grade: wide establishing shot, slow push-in, low warm sunlight, desaturated teal-orange
Write the physical elements that create the mood: thin mist, backlit rim light, wet-ground reflections, low ambience
Write how light and material behave: soft side light, controlled reflections, clean background, brushed-metal texture
Write physical scale: crowd size, camera distance, building height
Name which texture: frosted glass, light-absorbing velvet, paper fiber
Write the one visual contrast or reveal that stuns
Write the concrete behavior of color, composition, and light
Delete it, or replace with concrete spatial scale and headcount
Delete; resolution is a parameter, not a description
Delete; quality isn't requested into existence
Write the single most important visual detail
Name the transition: match cut, hard cut, whip pan

templates.name: Compact template
templates.desc: Reference image + change scope + camera + sound, said in one sentence
templates.text: @Image1 as reference, strictly keep [subject/product/face/logo] unchanged; only add [action/light/camera change]. Camera: [one action]. Sound: [SFX or ambience].

templates.name: Multimodal reference template
templates.desc: Image / video / audio each play their part — identity locked without copying the reference
templates.text: @Image1 locks the original character's identity and outfit. @Video1 provides camera movement only; do not copy its person, location, or brand. @Audio1 provides tempo and mood only.

templates.name: Timeline template
templates.desc: Long-prompt skeleton for 8+ seconds (common in the Jimeng/Dreamina community, field-observed)
templates.text:
[Style] [medium, texture, palette — one sentence]
[Timeline] 0-3s: [frame + camera + sound]; 3-6s: [frame + camera + sound]; 6-10s: [frame + camera + sound]
[Sound] [dialogue / ambience / SFX / no music]
[References] @Image1 locks subject identity; @Video1 camera movement only; @Audio1 tempo only

workedExample.bad: epic cinematic shot of a woman reading a letter, emotional, beautiful lighting
workedExample.good: Medium close-up, eye-level; she lowers the letter and her hands go still as a slow push-in arrives; soft window light behind her keeps her face plain; near-silence with one chair scrape — the realization lands in the stilled hands, not a word.
workedExample.note: Translate "emotion" into shot size, camera position, action, light, and sound, and the model knows what to emphasize.
